title: Traffic Flow Simulation with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D traffic flow simulation using Three.js (via CDN). The scene simulates vehicles as colored particles flowing along a multi-lane road network with realistic traffic dynamics.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 80, 100) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (0x404040, intensity 0.6) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) at (50, 100, 50).
- Dark background color (0x1a1a2e).
- Render a ground plane (200x200, color 0x2d2d2d).
- Create a road network: two straight roads crossing at the origin. Each road is 10 units wide with 2 lanes in each direction (4 lanes total per road). Road color: 0x444444. Draw white dashed lane markings.
- The horizontal road runs along the X-axis from -80 to 80. The vertical road runs along the Z-axis from -80 to 80.

## Vehicle Particles
- Represent each vehicle as a small BoxGeometry (1.5 x 0.5 x 1.0) mesh.
- Color-code by speed: green (>0.8 of max speed), yellow (0.4-0.8), red (<0.4).
- Maximum speed: 0.5 units per frame.
- Spawn vehicles at road entry points (edges of the map) with random lane assignments.
- Maintain a pool of up to 60 vehicles total.
- Vehicles follow their lane, slow down when approaching another vehicle (maintain minimum 3-unit gap), and stop at red traffic lights.
- When vehicles exit the map boundary (>85 units from center on their axis), remove and respawn them.

## Traffic Light System
- Place a traffic light at the intersection (origin). Represent it as a tall cylinder (post) with three sphere lights (red, yellow, green).
- Traffic light cycle: Green for horizontal road (8 seconds) -> Yellow (2 seconds) -> Red (then green for vertical road, 8 seconds) -> Yellow (2 seconds) -> repeat.
- Only the active light sphere should be emissive; others are dim (0x333333).
- Vehicles on the red-light road must stop before the intersection (at Z or X = -12 to -10 depending on direction).

## Particle Exhaust Effects
- Each vehicle emits small particle exhaust from its rear. Use a simple particle system: each vehicle has up to 5 tiny sphere particles (radius 0.15, semi-transparent gray) that fade out and drift upward over 1 second, then recycle.

## HUD / UI
- Display a HUD overlay (HTML div) showing:
  - 'Vehicles: {count}' — current active vehicle count
  - 'Avg Speed: {value}' — average speed of all vehicles (0.00 format)
  - 'Light: {H-Green|H-Yellow|V-Green|V-Yellow}' — current traffic light phase
  - 'Time: {seconds}' — simulation elapsed time in whole seconds
- Add three HTML buttons:
  - 'Pause/Resume' button (id='btn-pause') — toggles simulation pause
  - 'Add Traffic' button (id='btn-add') — increases spawn rate, adding 10 more vehicles to the max pool (cap at 120)
  - 'Clear Traffic' button (id='btn-clear') — removes all vehicles and resets count

## Keyboard Controls
- Press 'C' to toggle camera between top-down view (0, 120, 0) looking straight down and the default perspective view.
- Press 'F' to toggle fast-forward mode (2x simulation speed).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- vehicleCount: number of active vehicles (integer)
- maxVehicles: current max pool size (integer)
- avgSpeed: average speed of all vehicles (float, 2 decimal places)
- trafficPhase: string — one of 'H-Green', 'H-Yellow', 'V-Green', 'V-Yellow'
- phaseDuration: seconds elapsed in current phase (float)
- isPaused: boolean
- isFastForward: boolean
- cameraMode: 'perspective' | 'topdown'
- elapsedTime: total simulation time in seconds (float, not counting paused time)
- totalSpawned: total vehicles spawned since start (integer)
- intersectionQueueH: number of vehicles stopped/queued on horizontal road near intersection (integer)
- intersectionQueueV: number of vehicles stopped/queued on vertical road near intersection (integer)
- exhaustParticleCount: total active exhaust particles (integer)

Ensure the simulation runs smoothly at 60fps. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop.
physics_constraints: Vehicles must maintain minimum 3-unit following distance. Vehicles must stop at red lights before the intersection. Speed is clamped between 0 and 0.5 units/frame. Vehicles must stay within their assigned lane. Traffic light phases must follow strict timing: 8s green, 2s yellow per direction. Average speed must be non-negative and <= max speed. Vehicle count must never exceed maxVehicles.
